---
title: "Resources"
order: 83
---

This module cites one new verbatim source (NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, public domain) and one standard
named but never quoted (ISO 31000, a paid publication) — the same paraphrase-only handling this
curriculum already gives AABB Standards, GAMP 5, and ISO 19011. All links below were checked at
the time this page was written.

- **[NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, "Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and
  Organizations"](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-37r2.pdf)**
  (PDF, final, December 2018) — the actual document this lesson quotes from (via a saved,
  scoped excerpt in `sources/nist/`, never from memory). Curl-checked directly from this session:
  returns HTTP 200. Read it if you want RMF's full task-by-task detail — this lesson and the three
  that follow it quote only the subset saved in the excerpt.

- **[ISO 31000, "Risk management — Guidelines"](https://www.iso.org/standard/65694.html)** — ISO's
  own public listing page for the standard: scope and purchase information, not the standard's
  text itself, which is a paid publication never independently fetched or quoted anywhere in this
  curriculum. A direct check from this session returned HTTP 403 — ISO's own bot protection
  blocking this environment's proxy, the identical issue `designing-an-internal-audit-program`
  hit with ISO 19011's listing page, not a dead or incorrect link. Confirmed reachable instead
  through the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine: its availability API reports a live snapshot,
  HTTP 200, captured 2026-10-01, at
  [web.archive.org/web/20261001045002/https://www.iso.org/standard/65694.html](https://web.archive.org/web/20261001045002/https://www.iso.org/standard/65694.html).
  Worth a direct check yourself before relying on it. Useful for confirming ISO 31000 is real,
  current, and generally scoped — nothing on this page is blood-establishment-specific, and
  nothing from it is quoted in this lesson.

- **[Quality risk management](../../quality-system-essentials/quality-risk-management/index.qmd)**
  — this curriculum's own module on ICH Q9(R1), the third framework this lesson compares RMF and
  ISO 31000 against. Read it for the actual four-stage process and FMEA walkthrough, which this
  lesson deliberately doesn't re-teach.

- **[CertMike Explains NIST Risk Management Framework](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d8Z1RyhmRXg)**
  (Mike Chapple, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson: a plain-language
  tour of RMF from a well-known security-certification educator. Not produced by NIST (searched for
  an official NIST-channel RMF video; none could be found and verified), and not blood-specific.
  Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST CSRC: About the Risk Management Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf)**
  — NIST's own landing page for RMF, with pages for each step including Prepare. Read it when you
  want the authoritative, current description of the steps beyond the excerpt this lesson quotes.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST CSRC: RMF Quick Start Guides](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/rmf-quick-start-guides)**
  — NIST's short, step-by-step orientation material for RMF. Useful as a plain-language companion
  before modules 2 through 5 build each step. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1, "Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments"](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/30/r1/final)**
  — NIST's publication page for its dedicated risk-assessment guide, the closest NIST analogue to
  the "identify and assess" part of the shared motion. Read it if you want to see how a federal
  source treats risk assessment separately from the RMF steps. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST Cybersecurity Framework](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework)** — NIST's own hub for its
  Cybersecurity Framework, a different NIST framework from RMF. Worth a look so you can tell the two
  apart when someone says "the NIST framework." Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Q9(R1) Quality Risk Management](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/q9r1-quality-risk-management)**
  — FDA's guidance page for ICH Q9(R1), the third framework compared here, for the official
  version of what `quality-risk-management` teaches. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[ICH Quality Guidelines](https://www.ich.org/page/quality-guidelines)** — the harmonisation
  body's own index of its quality guidelines, including Q9. Use it to see where Q9 sits among the
  other quality guidelines. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
